newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU monetary committee meets on EMU blueprint.
newsitem.headline: EU monetary committee meets on EMU blueprint.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee met on Tuesday to hammer out remaining details over the blueprint for monetary union and lay the groundwork for a meeting of EU finance ministers on April 5.

EU monetary sources said the regularly scheduled gathering of national treasury and central bank officials would consider putting an agreed growth and stability pact for countries joining EMU into a legal context.
"This meeting is not really something spectacular," said one EU official. "It's more about the nitty gritty details of implementing a political decision."

In December, the EU agreed on a stability pact that would restrain budget deficits among countries joining the single currency. The accord includes stiff penalties for those running annual budget deficits over three percent of GDP.
The Dublin summit of EU leaders also agreed on a new Exchange Rate Mechanism, linking the single currency to those outside EMU in 1999, and a legal framework for monetary union.
Both the stability pact and the legal framework have to be enshrined into EU law, and it is the details of such a process that the monetary committee is considering.
Officials say they are unaware of trouble spots in any of these areas.

Where progress has been slowed, however, is in the adoption of a regulation on several aspects to the legal framework -- the name of the single currency, the euro, the continuity of financial contracts, rounding rules and the one-for-one conversion rate between the euro and the ecu.
At the Dublin summit is was agreed that these four issues would be put into a legal text early in the year, using Article 235 of the Maastricht treaty.
But because the article requires unanimity, it has been held up by Britain which wants to avoid endorsing any aspect of EMU until after its national election on May 1.
This is not being viewed as a large problem, since Britain has in principle agreed to everything in the regulation. EU officials said they expect adoption shortly after the British election.
